Good morning, Shahriaar. Today is Thursday, November 26. This is your morning brief.

Weather today is 8 degrees Celsius, clear skies. The high will be 18 and the low 7 degrees Celsius. Chance of precipitation is 0 percent.

You have 2 appointments in the next 24 hours: 11:00 AM, Regarding Mr. Niknejad; 11:00 AM, Meeting with Vitray Company.

Now, the top 2 stories in AI today.

First, from The Verge: FCC Approves SpaceX's Plan for Up to 1 Million AI Data Center Satellites. The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of its "Starmind" initiative, effectively approving AI data centers in space. The agency described it as the first approval of its kind, while Google and Blue Origin are also pursuing similar orbital data center concepts. The move places AI infrastructure in orbit and represents a major expansion of computing capacity beyond terrestrial data centers. Why it matters: Signals a new frontier in AI infrastructure, potentially enabling space-based AI computing and data processing at unprecedented scale.

Second, from TechCrunch: OpenAI Merges ChatGPT Chat and Work with Unified Usage Meter. OpenAI is merging the ChatGPT Chat and Work experiences into a single interface governed by one unified usage meter. The company warned that heavy ChatGPT users may reach usage limits sooner under the consolidated system. The change alters how consumers and enterprise customers access the chatbot and could affect usage patterns for OpenAI's flagship product as it unifies its consumer and business offerings. Why it matters: Directly impacts OpenAI's user base and enterprise customers by changing access patterns, usage limits, and the product experience for one of the most widely used AI chatbots.

That is your brief. Have a great day.
